column1: # Corrections applied to the entries go-licenses derives from the module graph,
#  - go-licenses resolves a licence from the file at the module root, which is
#    wrong for modules that licence parts of their tree differently;
#  - it resolves the directory of a nested major version, such as /v2, with a
#    network request, and without network access it picks the wrong one;
#  - when a module directory has no licence file, the module zip carries the
#    licence at the repository root, but go-licenses links the missing file;
#  - it does not see the C code that a package compiles with cgo.
# Tab-separated: module name, licence name, licence URL, note. {version} in the URL
# and in the note is replaced with the resolved module version. The note is
# optional. The script fails when a line matches no entry.

column4: only the library packages are used, that is, everything outside cmd/, and those are LGPL-3.0. The GPL-3.0 COPYING file at the module root covers go-ethereum's own binaries, which this project does not build or distribute.

built with cgo, this package also compiles the bundled libsecp256k1 C library, which is under the [MIT licence](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/{version}/crypto/secp256k1/libsecp256k1/COPYING)
